title: ETF Flow Pressure
market_behavior: Fund flows and model-portfolio reallocations can create gradual pressure in liquid ETFs and their underlying exposures.
forced_actor: Model-portfolio allocators, ETF flow followers, retirement platforms, volatility-budgeted portfolios, and benchmark-aware allocators.
why_edge_might_exist: Allocation decisions often happen over multiple sessions, so strong flow pressure may persist briefly after a signal becomes visible.
why_large_capital_may_ignore_it: Broad ETF flow effects are well known and crowded; smaller ETF variants may have limited capacity, lower absolute P&L, and annoying liquidity monitoring.
capacity_hypothesis: Capacity may be adequate for small personal accounts but should be bucketed by ETF dollar volume and spread before deployment.
data_required: group labels for ETF category comparisons
observable_predictions: Flow-sensitive ETF breakouts or trend states should retain enough return while reducing downside or improving risk-adjusted behavior.
The pattern should not rely on one symbol, one date window, or one cost assumption.
falsification_tests: Reject the exact implementation if cost sensitivity and date sensitivity fail.
Weaken the mechanism if multiple ETF groups fail under simple prespecified proxies.
Treat any result as proxy-only unless flow data or liquidity buckets support the mechanism.
references: Practitioner literature on ETF flows and allocation momentum
Academic literature on flow-induced price pressure
